note: Articolo sulla cocristallizzazione di teobromina (TBR) e teofillina (TPH) con acido piromellitico (PMLA) per sospensione lenta, macinazione e microonde. Gli eventi sono le prove di macinazione (neat e assistita da solvente) e di sospensione a microonde, l'analisi termica (STA) dei cinque sistemi e la desolvatazione/transizione del solvato col metanolo (VT-SXRD, TGA, DSC). Non estratto come evento: lo screening in soluzione (preparazioni), le dilatazioni termiche anisotrope del solvato col metanolo fra 300 e 415 K (nessun cambio di forma: sono in extra), i dati biologici e di solubilita' (le solubilita' sono in molecole; zone di inibizione nell'extra), le perdite di massa non assegnate dell'idrato (circa 12 % a 210-250 °C, circa 38 % fino a 335 °C) e del solvato (circa 7.5 % fino a 236 °C), il terzo picco DSC del cocristallo TBR·PMLA ('decomposition of the theobromine molecules', senza T). La frase delle conclusioni su TPH che 'can convert into a hydrated form' e' generale, senza condizioni: non e' un evento. CCDC 2427610-2427614 (cinque strutture a 134 K) e 2435404-2435414 (VT-SXRD) sono intervalli senza ordine dichiarato: restano nel campo ccdc dell'articolo, espansi in elenco. Incoerenze dell'articolo: (1) intervallo della VT-SXRD «from 300 to 425 K» nei metodi contro «300–415 K» nell'abstract e nei risultati; (2) nel polimorfo II i COOH···Nimidazole sono scritti «O2–H2···O4» invece di «O2–H2···N4»; (3) «the endo-carbonyl oxygen atom of the bromine» (refuso per theobromine); (4) la STA e' descritta con «a nitrogen purge (20 °C min–1) at a rate of 10 °C min–1»; (5) nella Tabella 1 la solubilita' dell'alcaloide puro e' data una volta per i tre sistemi di TPH (45.7).

citazioni: The use of water enabled the formation of the TBR·PMLA 2:1 cocrystal during a microwave reaction conducted at 125 °C for 10 min (Figure S7).
Water proved to be the most effective solvent for microwave-assisted cocrystallization of TBR and PMLA, with almost complete conversion of the substrates at 125 °C in 10 min.
Microwave cocrystallizations involving theobromine were performed using different solvents for 5 to 10 min at temperatures ranging from 100 to 175 °C (Table S5).

citazioni: A variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction experiment for a single crystal of TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 was performed in the 300–415 K temperature range.

The main objective was to investigate the solvent release process from the channels formed among components of this cocrystal solvate and how desolvation would affect the behavior of the single crystal.
An increase in the temperature causes the release of methanol molecules from the crystal lattice (Figure ), which is confirmed by both STA and X-ray structural analysis.
A change in the stoichiometry of the TPH·PMLA·MeOH cocrystal solvate from 2:1:2 to 2:1:1 is observed when the single crystal was heated to 390 K (Figure ).
Reflection intensities were collected from 300 to 425 K, with 10 K intervals within the 340–410 K temperature range.

citazioni: Heating the single crystal to 415 K causes a significant decrease in indexation and initial powdering of the crystal. At this stage, after performing data reduction for reflections with I/σ­(I) > 8, the structure refinement process showed the presence of two methanol molecules per unit cell.

Additionally, at the final stage of X-ray experiment, the crystal was heated to 420 K and a powder X-ray diffraction experiment was conducted (Figure ). The reflection positions for the obtained powder pattern coincide with the reflection positions of the TPH·PMLA 2:1 II cocrystal, which means that the desolvation process leads to the phase transition from the TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 cocrystal solvate into the TPH·PMLA 2:1 II cocrystal.
Comparison of theoretical powder patterns of the TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 (black) and TPH·PMLA 2:1 II (green) forms with the diffraction pattern obtained for the pulverized crystal at 420 K (red).

Additionally, a variable-temperature SXRD experiment, performed for the TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 single crystal in the 300–415 K range, revealed negative volumetric thermal expansion of this cocrystal solvate and a gradual solvent release, ultimately leading to a phase transition into the TPH·PMLA 2:1 II cocrystal.
Moreover, a phase transition to the TPH·PMLA 2:1 II form occurred, preceded by the gradual release of solvent molecules from TPH·PMLA·MeOH phase.

citazioni: Theobromine was obtained from Sigma-Aldrich. Theophylline (TPH) and pyromellitic acid (benzene-1,2,4,5-tetracarboxylic acid, PMLA) were purchased from TriMen Chemicals.
These reagents were used without prior purification (Figure ).

citazioni: Theobromine (TBR) and pyromellitic acid (PMLA) were dissolved in a methanol/water mixture at a 2:1 stoichiometric ratio by heating and stirring. The prepared solution was left for slow evaporation to obtain 2:1 TBR·PMLA single crystals.
preparazioni.note: Soluzione a caldo con agitazione («by heating and stirring»), poi evaporazione lenta: cristalli singoli del cocristallo 2:1. Dettagli delle condizioni di cristallizzazione nel supplementare (Tabella S1).

citazioni: Theophylline (TPH) and pyromellitic acid (PMLA) in a 2:1 stoichiometric ratio were dissolved by heating in a methanol-nitromethane mixture. After slow evaporation of this solution, single crystals of the TPH·PMLA 2:1 I cocrystal were obtained.
Cocrystallization of theophylline with pyromellitic acid in a stoichiometric ratio of 2:1 from a methanol/nitromethane mixture yielded polymorph I of TPH·PMLA 2:1.
preparazioni.note: Soluzione a caldo in metanolo-nitrometano, evaporazione lenta: cristalli singoli della forma I del 2:1.

citazioni: Polymorph TPH·PMLA 2:1 II was similarly obtained using a methanol-chloroform mixture.
Substituting nitromethane with chloroform resulted in polymorph II formation.
preparazioni.note: «Similarly» a F2: in metanolo-cloroformio al posto di metanolo-nitrometano (stesso rapporto 2:1, riscaldamento e evaporazione lenta).

citazioni: Single crystals in the form of large blocks of the TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 cocrystal solvate were identified for the first time from the cocrystallization of TPH with PMLA in a 4:1 stoichiometric ratio, conducted in a methanol-nitromethane solvent mixture.
preparazioni.note: Grandi blocchi cristallini del solvato col metanolo ottenuti la prima volta da TPH e PMLA 4:1 in metanolo-nitrometano.

citazioni: These crystals were used to nucleate the cocrystallization of TPH with PMLA in a 2:1 stoichiometric ratio in the same solvent mixture, yielding a pure cocrystal solvate.
preparazioni.note: I cristalli della preparazione precedente (4:1) servono da semi per la cocristallizzazione 2:1 nello stesso solvente: solvato puro. Il testo dice anche che la riproducibilita' e' difficile («difficulties with the repeatability of obtaining TPH·PMLA·MeOH 2:1:2 solvate»).

citazioni: The TPH·PMLA·H2O 1:1:2 cocrystal hydrate was obtained by cocrystallization of TPH and PMLA in a 1:1 stoichiometric ratio in an acetonitrile/water mixture, followed by slow evaporation of the solution.
The TPH·PMLA·H2O 1:1:2 cocrystal hydrate was successfully obtained through cocrystallization of TPH and PMLA in a 1:1 stoichiometric ratio from an acetonitrile–water system (Figure S2 and Table S1).
preparazioni.note: Idrato da TPH e PMLA 1:1 in acetonitrile/acqua, evaporazione lenta.

citazioni: Grindings were performed in the absence or with a small volume of solvent for 30 min to 2 h. In this way, TBR·PMLA 2:1 cocrystals, both TPH·PMLA 2:1 I and II cocrystal polymorphs and the TPH·PMLA·H2O 1:1:2 cocrystal hydrate were successfully synthesized.

Mechanochemical reactions were carried out using Retsch MM300 oscillatory ball mill in 3 mL stainless steel jars with one 6 mm stainless steel ball placed inside the jar at the constant frequency of 25 Hz.

citazioni: The use of microwave radiation shortened the cocrystallization process using TPH and PMLA to 5 min, enabling the successful formation of both polymorphs of the TPH·PMLA 2:1 cocrystal and TPH·PMLA·H2O 1:1:2.
Water proved to be the most effective solvent for microwave-assisted cocrystallization of TBR and PMLA, with almost complete conversion of the substrates at 125 °C in 10 min.
